summary: Medicine Point Lookout, a CCC-era L-4 cab in Montana's Bitterroot Mountains staffed into 1976, was restored in 1999 and is now a hike-in Forest Service rental.

facts.design: L-4 cab, pyramid roof, on an 8-10 foot wood/pole tower

access.note: Forest Service rental via Recreation.gov; hike-in only, no vehicle access.

visit.trail_note: 3.5-mile hike with about 2,000 feet of elevation gain; no ATVs/OHVs; horses allowed.

events.note: NHLR: tower constructed by the CCC in 1930.
NHLR: pyramid roof L-4 cab added atop the tower.
Firelookout.com gives 1940 as the build year for the L-4 cab on a 10-foot pole tower (conflicts with NHLR's 1930/1933 dates).
Earliest recorded lookout staff: Mr. and Mrs. Raymond Barnett.
Last recorded staffing year, lookout Rene Eustace.
Tower restored; NHLR registration dated October 8, 1999.

evidence.supports: 1930 CCC construction, 1933 cab, 1930 tower, 8-foot height, restoration 1999
evidence.quote: Constructed in 1930 by the CCC, the lookout is located in the Bitterroot Mountains 15 miles south of Darby. It is a 1933 pyramid roof, 14' x 14' L-4 cab with catwalk atop an 8' wood tower. Last staffed in 1976, the lookout was restored in 1999.

evidence.supports: 1940 build date, 10-foot pole tower, staffing roster through 1976
evidence.quote: Built in 1940, this 10' pole tower with L-4 cab was used sporadically in the 1980's... Known lookout personnel: 1946: Mr. and Mrs. Raymond Barnett;... 1976: Rene Eustace.

evidence.supports: 1939 period of significance on NRHP nomination
evidence.quote:
Periods Of Significance:
1939 AD - 1967 AD
Significant Years:
1939

evidence.supports: restored to 1940s appearance, cab dimensions, catwalk, hike-in access, no water, wood stove
evidence.quote: It has been restored to reflect a lookout of the 1940s, including the stove, furniture, dishes and other small touches... The lookout measures 14ft.X14ft. with a 30 inch catwalk around the outside... There is no water available near the lookout

evidence.supports: 3.5-mile hike, 2000 ft elevation gain, no ATVs, horses allowed
evidence.quote: The tower is accessed by a somewhat difficult 3.5-mile hike from the parking area with a 2,000 foot elevation gain... horses and other livestock are welcome.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR dates construction to 1930 (CCC) with the L-4 cab added in 1933; Firelookout.com instead states the whole structure was built in 1940. The NRHP nomination's 1939 period-of-significance date falls between the two and does not clearly resolve it. The story reports both figures and flags the disagreement rather than picking one.

sources.title: National Register of Historic Places nomination (Asset 100002298)

notes_for_editor: Build year is genuinely unresolved between NHLR (1930/1933) and firelookout.com (1940); the NRHP nomination's 'significant years' field (1939) was only partially legible in the crawl cache and did not include a clear text statement to resolve it, so I did not treat it as deciding the question. Firelookout.com's staffing list also includes a 1958 Mr. and Mrs. Dale Dye entry that had been omitted from the story; added it for completeness.
